odometer_gate.verdict_raw: SIGNAL SOUND -- camera static, agent active (all four gate calls)

asm_cpu_cross_check.why: task instructions: a completely-flat trace under every direction must be checked against the ASM-CPU NMI-batching anomaly (docs/research/LEAGUE_ONBOARDING_WAVE4_2026-08-25.md headline finding) before concluding CAMERA_STATIC, by constructing nes_core.NESEnvironment directly (interpreter-only, no ASM-CPU toggle) the same way the Journey to Silius attempt did.
asm_cpu_cross_check.method: held RIGHT for 1200 steps (frame_skip=4) from the exact same start state via nes_core.NESEnvironment(...) directly (bypassing Pool/ASM-CPU entirely), tracking env.get_odometer() every step.
asm_cpu_cross_check.result: range x=0 y=0 -- IDENTICAL to the Pool/ASM-CPU result. The interpreter-only path and the ASM-CPU path AGREE (both flat), unlike Journey to Silius where they DISAGREED (interpreter showed real scroll, ASM-CPU was flat).
asm_cpu_cross_check.conclusion: NOT the ASM-CPU flat-trace anomaly. The PPU scroll register genuinely never moves under a simple held-single-direction driver in this game. Consistent with the sibling DD1 profile's own documented precedent (configs/double_dragon.yaml): a combat-gated brawler whose camera locks per fight zone and only advances the PPU scroll on a real room-clear transition, which a static single-direction 1200-step probe never reaches.
